profile.org_note: Congressionally chartered nonprofit governed by a board of federal financial-regulator and HUD officials (FDIC, NCUA, OCC, HUD seats; two seats turned over in 2026 and the board elected a temporary chair in September 2026). Five corporate officers (CEO, COO, CFO, General Counsel, CIO) sit above divisions for Field Operations (four regions, each with a vice president and a senior director), National Initiatives, Training, Organizational Assessment and finance. There is no land acquisition or land development function at all: the homes are built by the independent local member nonprofits, each with its own board and executive director, and any land decision is made locally.
profile.summary: NOT a conventional for-sale homebuilder. NeighborWorks America is a congressionally chartered national nonprofit (Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation, Washington, DC) that gives federal grant money, training and oversight to a network of 248 independent local nonprofits; its Builder 100 entry (No. 72 in 2026) simply adds up the for-sale homes those members built and sold. It owns no land, controls no lots and has no land or capital-markets staff, so it is not a plausible land-banking customer itself; any lot deal would be with an individual member nonprofit, and those are small, subsidy-driven and already served by two affiliated nonprofit lenders (Community Housing Capital and NeighborWorks Capital).
